demo.text: You've put AI agents on Kubernetes. They can read logs, check rollouts, and find the cause.
But they only work when someone opens a prompt and asks.
Alerts fire in your monitoring. Questions come up in chat. Your agents hear neither.
Introducing Agent Kourier: a Kubernetes-native broker between team chat and A2A agents.
An alert, or a question, becomes an agent session, in the thread where it landed. Slack today.
When an alert lands in the channel, Agent Kourier picks it up, opens the thread, and hands it to your agent. It investigates right there, step by step, and reports what it found.
Reply in the thread, and the same session continues. Same context, nothing re-explained.
Or skip the alert, and just ask.
When the agent needs a decision, it asks, and waits for your answer.
And if Agent Kourier restarts mid-answer, the thread still finishes, and no incoming message is lost.
Teams add one Binding, in YAML, next to their agent. The platform wiring is shared.

It works with kagent, or any A2A agent that streams. It's a two-way session: it answers as it works, asks when it needs you, and keeps the context when you reply. Slack today; more chat platforms are planned. Agent Kourier. Write the agent, not the chat integration.

teaser.text: Your agent is ready. The chat integration is another project.
